assertions: Native token semantic values and clone/equality fields remain matched by explicit projections of unmodified original evidence.
Native JavaScript references preserve FAP original identity without token acquire/release/delete or custom memory management.

stackDivergence.rationale: Task82 user-authorized browser adaptation removes the Boost intrusive_ptr runtime, token ownership counters/policies and acquire/release/delete hooks. FormulaTokenRef and FormulaConstTokenRef are nullable native JS references; FormulaFAPToken retains its original token directly, including across Clone. JS GC owns ordinary token lifetime. Semantic token values/opcodes/types/equality, independent payload clones and FAP identity remain original-shaped. Existing SAL/SVL shared-value cleanup API is unchanged and does not cascade through FAP references; this is not a global shared-string memory migration. Original immutable native captures remain intact; comparison explicitly projects only C++ token count/policy fields, and obsolete pointer-manager lifecycle assertions are replaced by meaningful live-alias/clone tests. No WeakRef/FinalizationRegistry, allocator, new pointer class, ownership counter or pretend GC timing is introduced. Future unported GetRef-based reuse algorithms must be adapted to protect aliases through semantic copying. Original physical lifetime/count/policy/ABI and full compiler/document/UI remain outside parity claims.
